title: PLC+ — foundations (preview)
note: Preview content for the instructors' review: modules 1-5 are first drafts, 6 an outline, 7-12 coming later. Challenges marked example are the machines on the Example tabs, like the exercises' machines but not the same ones (D21).

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Three rungs: one contact for Green, two in series (AND) for Amber, a normally closed contact for Red.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: Red uses a normally open contact, so it lights in Auto instead of Manual.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Rung 1: Start, or the Motor's own contact in parallel with it (the seal-in), passes power through Stop to the Motor coil. Let go of Start and the seal-in keeps the motor running. Stop is wired normally closed (TRUE until pressed), so the program checks it with a normally open contact: pressing Stop opens it and breaks the circuit.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: Rung 1 has no seal-in contact: the motor runs only while Start is held down.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Three on-delay timers in a chain, each started by the one before finishing; the last one restarts the first.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: Yellow has nothing to turn it off when red comes on, so the two are on together.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Two start/stop circuits, one per direction, each stopped by its limit switch and locked out by the other; the down rung also needs the safety eye clear.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: The down rung does not check the safety eye, so the door comes down on whatever is in the doorway.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Two latched memory tags, Filling and Draining, set and reset by the floats; the valves follow them.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: Without memory, the valves follow the high float alone: the tank chatters around 80 % and never drains.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: The metal sensor latches MetalSeen; the diverter pushes when the photo-eye sees a part and MetalSeen is set; the part leaving the eye resets it.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: The diverter pushes every part that reaches the eye, metal or plastic.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Three rungs: Ready follows the guard; Press closing needs Left hand AND Right hand AND the guard shut (three contacts in series); Guard open uses a normally closed contact (NOT).

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: The two hand buttons are side by side (OR), so the press closes with one hand on a button: the other hand could be under it.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Rung 1: PumpStart, or the pump's own contact beside it (the seal-in), through PumpStop and OverloadOK to the Pump coil. Both are wired normally closed, so normally open contacts pass power until Stop is pressed or the overload trips. Rung 2 lights the lamp.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: PumpStop is checked with a normally closed contact. The button is wired normally closed (TRUE while not pressed), so that contact is open all the time and the pump never starts. The most common mistake with Stop buttons.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Two start/stop circuits with seal-ins. Each has a normally closed contact of the other direction (the interlock), so only one can be on.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: There is no interlock: press Reverse while the motor runs forward, and both contactors are told to pull in at once.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Overheat sets a memory tag, Alarm; ResetPB AND NOT Overheat resets it. The light and the horn follow Alarm, so the alarm stays on until someone resets it.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: The light and the horn follow the temperature switch directly. The moment the oven cools, the alarm clears itself, and nobody knows it was ever too hot.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Rung 1 turns the press into a one-scan Pulse with a rising-edge contact (ONS on Allen-Bradley). Rung 2 flips the light on each Pulse.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: Without the edge, Pulse is TRUE for every scan the button is held (one scan is 10 ms), so the light flips on and off many times a press and ends up wherever it happens to stop.
